## Story

As a release engineer gating Phase 4 migration cutover on a multi-workflow coherence check, I can run a six-chunk multi-opus workflow coherence walkthrough that dispatches six independent opus-tier analyses across the brainstorm / preplanning / implementation-plan / sprint / commit-and-review / operational-dry-run surfaces, each producing structured JSON evidence and a PASS/AMBIGUOUS/FAIL verdict — so any FAIL or AMBIGUOUS finding blocks Phase 4 until resolved (spec amendment, prompt fix, or explicit defer decision).

This story re-implements epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 SC10 at the full scope specified in the epic. The existing `coherence-walk.sh` (a Phase 1 heuristic) is **not** the SC10 implementation — it is a deterministic regex-based scanner for transitional language and SC/CC overlap that runs in `validate.sh`. This story builds the multi-opus workflow walkthrough that SC10 actually specifies.

## Done Definitions (verbatim from epic SC10)

- DD1 (six parallel chunks): The walkthrough dispatches six opus-tier analyses **in parallel** (single message with six Agent tool calls). Chunks:
  - **Chunk A (brainstorm)**: reads `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/brainstorm/` SKILL.md + phases/* + prompts/*; validates the brainstorm dialogue produces correct end-state-vs-Closure-Checks separation; verifies the new verifiable-sc-check rule is enforced; verifies approval gate output is well-formed.
  - **Chunk B (preplanning)**: reads `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/preplanning/` SKILL.md + prompts/* + docs/reviewers/*; validates story decomposition preserves the SC/Closure-Checks distinction at the story level; validates done-definitions inherit end-state-only semantics.
  - **Chunk C (implementation-plan)**: reads `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/implementation-plan/` SKILL.md + prompts/* + docs/reviewers/*; validates task decomposition produces AC + Closure Checks correctly.
  - **Chunk D (sprint)**: reads `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/sprint/` SKILL.md + prompts/* + the completion-verifier dispatch path; validates execution sub-agents consume the schema; verifies completion-verifier subtree walk integrates correctly with the sprint closure flow.
  - **Chunk E (commit-and-review)**: reads `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/workflows/COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md` + REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md + all code-reviewer-*.md agents; validates review surfaces Closure Checks failures distinctly from end-state failures.
  - **Chunk F (operational-dry-run)**: runs the classification-preview script (see Brainstorm Decisions §3) against the 10 most recently closed `brainstorm:complete`-tagged epics; per epic, records the count of items that would have been flagged as transitional under the new schema; documents as before/after evidence that the migration prevents future false-positive closures. Note: chunk F does NOT dispatch the completion-verifier agent — see Brainstorm Decisions §3 for rationale.

- DD2 (per-chunk JSON output): Each chunk produces structured JSON conforming to `{workflow_stage: "brainstorm" | "preplanning" | "implementation-plan" | "sprint" | "commit-and-review" | "operational-dry-run", status: "PASS" | "AMBIGUOUS" | "FAIL", evidence_citations: [{file: <path>, line: <int>}], findings: [{severity, description, recommendation}], tech_failure: <bool, optional, defaults false>}`. Schema documented in a contract doc at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/contracts/coherence-walkthrough-chunk-output.md`. The `tech_failure: true` variant is set by the orchestrator when retry-on-failure exhausts (see Brainstorm Decisions §2).

- DD3 (aggregated report): An aggregated report combining all six chunks is attached as a comment to the epic ticket being gated, in the format documented in the contract doc. Report includes a summary table (per-chunk verdict) + the full per-chunk JSON.

- DD4 (Phase 4 blocking gate): Any FAIL or AMBIGUOUS finding from any chunk blocks Phase 4 migration until resolved. Resolution paths: (a) spec amendment recorded as an Operational Constraints amendment comment on the epic; (b) prompt fix that addresses the underlying chunk failure; (c) explicit defer decision recorded as a comment. The gate re-runs after resolution and must report all-PASS to unblock. A chunk classified `tech_failure: true` is treated as AMBIGUOUS for blocking purposes.

- DD5 (relationship to Phase 1 heuristic): The walkthrough does NOT replace `coherence-walk.sh` (the Phase 1 heuristic). The heuristic runs in `validate.sh` on every change. The Phase 2 multi-opus walkthrough runs at Phase 4 gate time on the specific epic being migrated. Both gates must pass.

← Validates Closure Check: "the multi-opus coherence walkthrough is invokable, runs the six chunks in parallel, and emits the contracted JSON + aggregated-report comment"
← Satisfies: "SC10: Multi-opus-agent workflow coherence walk-through gated between Phase 3 (audit and pointer updates complete) and Phase 4 (migration). Six parallel chunks (A-F as specified), each opus-tier, each producing structured JSON {workflow_stage, status, evidence_citations, findings}. Aggregated report attached to ticket. Any FAIL or AMBIGUOUS finding blocks Phase 4 migration until resolved (spec amendment, prompt fix, or explicit defer decision)."

## Brainstorm Decisions (locked 2026-05-20)

These four decisions resolve the design ambiguity flagged by the `scrutiny:pending` tag. All decisions stay within the scope of SC10 — no scope expansion beyond what the epic requires.

### §1. Reuse profile: one-shot, lightly parameterized

The walkthrough is built for the a03c Phase 4 cutover. The script accepts an `--epic-id` argument (so the same code could in principle gate a future schema migration), but it has **no** profile-schema framework, **no** per-chunk cost-ceiling enforcement, **no** caching layer, and **no** path-based trigger hook. Rationale: YAGNI / Rule of Three — there is no concrete second consumer, and a future migration epic can refactor only when it actually exists.

### §2. Prompt structure: shared verdict rubric + six chunk prompts

One shared rubric file at `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/verdict-rubric.md` defines PASS / AMBIGUOUS / FAIL semantics, the JSON output contract, citation format, and refusal-to-invent-findings discipline. Each of the six chunks has its own short prompt file (`prompts/chunk-a-brainstorm.md` through `prompts/chunk-f-operational-dry-run.md`) that opens by reading the rubric and then appends chunk-specific instructions (which files to read, what validation property to evaluate, 2-3 worked accept/reject examples).

Rationale: keeps verdict semantics aligned across chunks (single source of truth for PASS/AMBIGUOUS/FAIL) without inventing a profile-schema abstraction.

### §3. Chunk F mechanism: targeted classification-preview script

Chunk F does NOT dispatch the completion-verifier agent. Instead, a small standalone script — `plugins/dso/scripts/closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` — lists the 10 most recent `brainstorm:complete`-tagged closed epics, runs the haiku classifier (the same one built by story ad70-f38a-7684-4e00) on each SC/DoD/AC item, and outputs `{epic_id, items_total, items_classified_transitional, items_classified_end_state, items_classified_uncertain}` per epic.

The chunk F opus prompt receives this script's output as input and produces a verdict on whether the before/after counts support the claim that the migration prevents future false-positive closures.

Rationale: Chunk F's purpose per the epic SC10 spec is "before/after evidence that the migration prevents future false-positive closures." This is a classification-preview task, not a full verification task. The completion-verifier agent has no native dry-run mode; rather than scope-creep into adding one, build a targeted script that does exactly what's needed and nothing more.

### §4. Dispatch failure policy: auto-retry once → persistent tech-failure becomes AMBIGUOUS

When an opus dispatch returns no parseable PASS/AMBIGUOUS/FAIL verdict (timeout, malformed JSON, rate-limit exhausted), the orchestrator retries that chunk once. On second failure, the chunk is recorded with `status: "AMBIGUOUS"` and `tech_failure: true` and a finding describing the technical error. AMBIGUOUS blocks Phase 4 (per DD4) — so a tech-failure forces human resolution before migration, but it doesn't conflate "the workflow has a real misalignment" with "the API call broke."

## Approach Summary

Build a thin orchestrator script (`plugins/dso/scripts/coherence-walkthrough.sh`) that:
1. Accepts `--epic-id <id>` (parameterized per §1)
2. Pre-flight: runs `closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` to produce chunk F's input data
3. Dispatches six opus Agent calls in a single Bash batch via the orchestrator (the script emits the prompt files and dispatch instructions; the actual Agent tool calls are made by the calling skill, not by the script). See `epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md` line 276 for the precedent multi-agent dispatch pattern (3-call → extends to 6-call).
4. Collects six JSON outputs (with one retry per failing chunk per §4)
5. Aggregates into the report shape documented in `coherence-walkthrough-chunk-output.md`
6. Attaches the aggregated report as a comment to the epic
7. Returns exit 0 if all-PASS, exit 1 if any chunk is FAIL or AMBIGUOUS (blocking Phase 4)

The script does NOT modify completion-verifier.md or any agent file. It does NOT add a continuous trigger. It is a one-shot gate invoked from sprint Phase G or manually before running `migrate-closure-checks.sh` Phase 4.

## Relevant Files

Files this story creates:
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/verdict-rubric.md` — shared PASS/AMBIGUOUS/FAIL rubric, JSON contract, citation format
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-a-brainstorm.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-b-preplanning.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-c-implementation-plan.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-d-sprint.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-e-commit-and-review.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/coherence-walk/prompts/chunk-f-operational-dry-run.md`
- `plugins/dso/scripts/coherence-walkthrough.sh` — orchestrator entry point
- `plugins/dso/scripts/closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` — chunk F pre-flight script
- `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/coherence-walkthrough-chunk-output.md` — JSON schema and aggregated-report contract

Files this story reads (does not modify):
- `plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` + `skills/brainstorm/phases/*` + `skills/brainstorm/prompts/*` (chunk A input)
- `plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/SKILL.md` + `skills/preplanning/prompts/*` + `skills/preplanning/docs/reviewers/*` (chunk B input)
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/SKILL.md` + similar (chunk C input)
- `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md` + `skills/sprint/prompts/*` + `plugins/dso/agents/completion-verifier.md` (chunk D input)
- `plugins/dso/docs/workflows/COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md` + `REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md` + `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-*.md` (chunk E input)
- The 10 most recent `brainstorm:complete`-tagged closed epics (chunk F input via preview script)
- `plugins/dso/scripts/coherence-walk.sh` (Phase 1 heuristic — DD5 relationship is documented; no modification)

Existing precedents this story builds on:
- `plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md` line 276 — 3-agent parallel dispatch pattern (extends to 6)
- `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh` — Phase 1 structural migration (this gate runs before its Phase 4 successor)

## Considerations (post-brainstorm — resolved status)

- **Brainstorming required before implementation-plan**: ✅ RESOLVED — all four open design questions answered above. Ready for `/dso:implementation-plan`.
- **Per-chunk prompt design**: ✅ RESOLVED — shared rubric + six prompts (§2).
- **Dispatch coordination / aggregation**: ✅ RESOLVED — retry-once → AMBIGUOUS (§4).
- **API cost**: 6 opus dispatches per walkthrough run + 1 haiku classifier batch for chunk F preview. At a single Phase 4 cutover, this is a bounded one-time cost. Document the per-run estimate in `coherence-walkthrough.sh --help`.
- **Phase 1 heuristic interaction**: ✅ DOCUMENTED in DD5 — complementary, both must pass.
- **Operational-dry-run (chunk F) data**: ✅ RESOLVED — does NOT use completion-verifier dry-run (none exists); uses targeted preview script (§3).

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
